syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Concept of management: effectiveness and efficiency

concepts.learning_objective: Define management as a process of getting things done to achieve goals effectively and efficiently.
Distinguish effectiveness (achieving goals) from efficiency (minimum cost of inputs) and explain why both must be balanced.
Identify management as goal-oriented, all pervasive, continuous and a group activity.
Describe the three dimensions of management: work, people and operations.
Explain why management is a dynamic function and an intangible force.
Explain survival, profit and growth as the organisational (economic) objectives of management.
Explain the social and personal objectives of management and the need to reconcile them with organisational goals.
Explain how management helps achieve group and personal goals, increases efficiency and develops society.
Explain how management helps people adapt to change so that the organisation stays competitive.

topics.title: Nature of management: art, science and profession
topics.ncert_sections: Nature of Management; Management as an Art; Management as a Science; Management as a Profession

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how management satisfies the features of an art.
Explain why management is an inexact science and how art and science complement each other.
Evaluate how far management meets the features of a profession.
Describe the role and tasks of top management.
Describe the role of middle management as the link between top and supervisory levels.
Describe the role of supervisory or operational management in overseeing the workforce.
Identify planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling from their descriptions.
Explain why management functions are interrelated rather than performed in isolation.

topics.title: Coordination: the essence of management
topics.ncert_sections: Coordination - The Essence of Management; Characteristics of Coordination; Importance of Coordination

concepts.learning_objective: Explain coordination as the force that binds all functions and the essence of management.
Describe the characteristics of coordination.
Explain how growth in size, functional differentiation and specialisation create the need for coordination.
Define a principle of management and explain why it is less rigid than a principle of pure science.
Distinguish principles of management from techniques of management and from values.
Explain the universal applicability of management principles and why they are only general guidelines.
Explain how management principles are flexible, contingent on the situation and mainly behavioural.
Explain that management principles are formed by practice and experimentation and show cause and effect relationships.
Explain how principles give managers insights into reality and help in optimum use of resources and effective administration.
Explain how principles support scientific decisions and help managers meet a changing environment.
Explain the role of principles in fulfilling social responsibility and in management training, education and research.

topics.title: Taylor's Principles of Scientific Management
topics.ncert_sections: Taylor's Scientific Management; Principles of Scientific Management

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Taylor replaced the rule of thumb with a scientifically developed one best method.
Explain the principles of harmony, not discord, and cooperation, not individualism.
Explain the principle of development of each and every person to his or her greatest efficiency and prosperity.
Describe functional foremanship and the roles of the eight specialist foremen.
Explain standardisation, simplification and the method, motion, time and fatigue studies.
Apply Taylor's differential piece wage system to compute and compare workers' earnings.

topics.title: Fayol's Principles: Division of Work to Remuneration

concepts.learning_objective: Explain division of work, authority and responsibility, and discipline as stated by Fayol.
Distinguish between unity of command and unity of direction and identify their violation.
Apply the principles of subordination of individual interest to general interest and fair remuneration.

topics.title: Fayol's Principles: Centralisation to Esprit de Corps; Fayol versus Taylor
topics.ncert_sections: Fayol's Principles of Management (viii) to (xiv); Fayol Versus Taylor

concepts.learning_objective: Explain centralisation and decentralisation, the scalar chain and the gang plank.
Identify the principles of order, equity, stability of personnel, initiative and esprit de corps in situations.
Compare the contributions of Fayol and Taylor on the bases given in the chapter.

topics.title: Meaning and features of business environment

concepts.learning_objective: Define business environment as the sum total of external individuals, institutions and forces that may affect a firm's performance.
Identify the features of business environment such as inter-relatedness, dynamic nature, uncertainty, complexity and relativity.
Distinguish specific forces that affect a firm directly from general forces that affect all firms.
Explain how understanding the environment helps a firm spot opportunities early and treat threats as warning signals.
Explain how business environment helps in tapping resources, coping with change, planning and improving performance.
Identify economic factors such as interest rates, inflation and disposable income and their effect on business.
Identify social forces such as customs, traditions, values and social trends and the opportunities they create.
Explain how scientific improvements and innovations create new products and make old ones obsolete.
Explain how political stability and the attitude of government towards business affect business confidence.
Explain how laws, administrative orders and court judgments regulate business activities.

topics.title: Economic environment in India and the New Industrial Policy, 1991
topics.ncert_sections: Economic Environment in India; Crisis of June 1991

concepts.learning_objective: Describe India's economic environment at Independence and the role given to the public and private sectors under planning.
State the main features of the New Industrial Policy of July 1991 and the crisis that led to it.
Explain liberalisation as freeing Indian industry from unnecessary controls and licensing.
Explain privatisation and disinvestment as giving a greater role to the private sector.
Explain globalisation as the integration of national economies into a cohesive global economy.
State the meaning, aims and features of demonetisation announced in November 2016.
Interpret the impact of demonetisation on savings, private wealth, real estate and tax collection.

topics.title: Impact of government policy changes on business and industry

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse the impact of liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation on Indian business and industry.
Explain market orientation as producing goods after studying market needs.
State the meaning of planning as deciding in advance what to do and how to do it.
Explain that planning covers both ends (objectives) and means (courses of action) within a time frame.
Describe how planning provides direction, reduces uncertainty and waste, promotes innovation and aids decision making.
Explain why planning establishes the standards needed for controlling.
Explain that planning is purposeful and is the primary function of management.
Explain that planning is pervasive across levels and departments and is a continuous process.
Explain that planning is futuristic, involves decision making and is a mental exercise.
Explain how rigidity and a dynamic environment limit the usefulness of plans.
Explain how planning may reduce creativity, involve huge costs and consume time.
Explain why planning does not guarantee success.
Describe setting objectives and developing premises as the first steps of planning.
Distinguish identifying, evaluating and selecting alternative courses of action.
Describe implementing the plan and follow-up action.

topics.title: Single-use and standing plans
topics.ncert_sections: Types of Plans: Single-use and standing plans

concepts.learning_objective: Identify single-use plans as plans for one-time, non-recurring situations.
Identify standing plans as plans for recurring activities, including policies, procedures, methods and rules.

topics.title: Objectives, strategy, policy, procedure, method, rule, programme and budget
topics.ncert_sections: Types of Plans: Objectives to Budget

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish objectives as desired end results from strategy as a comprehensive long-term plan.
Distinguish policies, procedures, methods and rules as guides to action.
Explain programmes as detailed project statements and budgets as numerical plans that also aid control.

topics.title: Meaning and process of organising
topics.ncert_sections: Meaning; Steps in the process of organising

concepts.learning_objective: Explain organising as the process that implements plans by clarifying jobs, working relationships and resources.
Sequence and identify the four steps in the process of organising.
Explain how organising brings specialisation, clarity in relationships, optimum use of resources and effective administration.
Explain how organising helps an enterprise adapt to change, develop personnel and grow.

topics.title: Organisation structure and span of management

concepts.learning_objective: Define organisation structure and explain why it must be reviewed as an enterprise grows.
Explain span of management and how it shapes the levels of management.

topics.title: Functional and divisional structures
topics.ncert_sections: Types of organisation structures: functional structure, divisional structure

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the functional structure with its advantages, disadvantages and suitability.
Describe the divisional structure with its advantages, disadvantages and suitability.
Choose between a functional and a divisional structure for a given business situation.
State the features, advantages and limitations of formal organisation.
State the features, merits and demerits of informal organisation and how management should treat it.

topics.title: Delegation
topics.ncert_sections: Delegation; Elements of delegation; Importance of delegation

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish authority, responsibility and accountability by meaning, origin, flow and delegability.
Explain the importance of delegation for managers, employees and the organisation.

topics.title: Decentralisation
topics.ncert_sections: Decentralisation; Centralisation and decentralisation; Importance; Delegation and decentralisation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain decentralisation and why centralisation and decentralisation are relative terms.
Explain the importance of decentralisation and apply it to business situations.
Distinguish between delegation and decentralisation.
Define staffing as the function of filling and keeping filled the positions in the organisation structure.
State the benefits that proper staffing brings to an organisation.

topics.title: Staffing as part of Human Resource Management
topics.ncert_sections: Staffing as part of Human Resource Management, Evolution of Human Resource Management

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the specialised duties performed by human resource personnel.
Trace the evolution from labour welfare officer to personnel manager to human resource manager.
Explain why staffing is both a line and a staff activity.
Explain how workload and workforce analysis estimate manpower requirements.
Describe the steps of the staffing process from recruitment to placement and orientation.
Distinguish between time based, performance based and indirect compensation.

topics.title: Recruitment and its sources
topics.ncert_sections: Recruitment, Sources of Recruitment, Internal Sources, External Sources

concepts.learning_objective: Define recruitment and distinguish it from selection.
Explain transfers and promotions with the merits and limitations of internal sources.
Choose suitable external sources of recruitment and state their merits and limitations.
Distinguish between intelligence, aptitude, personality, trade and interest tests.
Describe the steps of the selection process in their proper order.

topics.title: Training and development
topics.ncert_sections: Training and Development, Importance of Training and Development, Training, Development and Education

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between training, development and education.
State the benefits of training to the organisation and to the employee.

topics.title: Training methods
topics.ncert_sections: Training Methods, On the Job Methods, Off the Job Methods

concepts.learning_objective: Explain apprenticeship, coaching, internship and job rotation as on-the-job methods.
Explain vestibule training, computer modelling and other off-the-job methods.

topics.title: Meaning, Characteristics, Importance and Principles of Directing
topics.ncert_sections: Meaning; Importance of Directing; Principles of Directing

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the meaning of directing and its characteristics: it initiates action, is continuous, takes place at every level and flows from top to bottom.
Explain how directing initiates action, integrates efforts, realises potential, eases change and brings stability.
Apply the principles of directing such as unity of command, harmony of objectives and appropriateness of direction technique.

topics.title: Elements of Directing and Supervision
topics.ncert_sections: Elements of Direction; Supervision; Importance of Supervision

concepts.learning_objective: Identify supervision, motivation, leadership and communication as the four elements of directing.
Distinguish supervision as an element of directing from supervision as the function of the supervisor at the operative level.
Explain the roles of a supervisor such as linking workers and management, maintaining group unity and training workers.

topics.title: Motivation: Concepts, Features, Process and Importance
topics.ncert_sections: Motivation; Features of Motivation; Motivation Process; Importance of Motivation

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between a motive, motivation and a motivator.
Explain the features of motivation and the sequence of the motivation process from unsatisfied need to reduction of tension.
Explain how motivation improves performance, changes attitudes and reduces turnover, absenteeism and resistance to change.

topics.title: Maslow's Need Hierarchy Theory
topics.ncert_sections: Maslow's Need Hierarchy Theory of Motivation

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the five levels of needs in Maslow's hierarchy with their organisational examples.
Apply the assumptions of Maslow's theory to explain why a satisfied need no longer motivates.
Identify financial incentives such as pay, bonus, profit sharing, stock options, retirement benefits and perquisites.
Identify non-financial incentives such as status, job enrichment, recognition, job security and empowerment, and explain their basis.

topics.title: Leadership
topics.ncert_sections: Leadership; Features and Importance of Leadership; Leadership Style

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the meaning, features and importance of leadership in an organisation.
Distinguish autocratic, democratic and laissez-faire leadership styles on the basis of the use of authority.

topics.title: Communication: Process, Formal and Informal Communication
topics.ncert_sections: Communication; Elements of Communication Process; Formal and Informal Communication

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the elements of the communication process such as encoding, media, decoding, feedback and noise.
Classify formal communication as upward, downward or horizontal and identify formal communication networks.
Explain the nature of informal (grapevine) communication and its networks.

topics.title: Barriers to Communication and Improving Communication Effectiveness
topics.ncert_sections: Barriers to Communication; Improving Communication Effectiveness

concepts.learning_objective: Identify semantic barriers such as technical jargon, unclarified assumptions and faulty translations.
Classify psychological, organisational and personal barriers to communication.
Suggest measures such as ensuring feedback to improve communication effectiveness.
State the meaning of controlling as ensuring that activities are performed as per plans.
Explain why controlling is a goal-oriented and pervasive function of management.
Explain why controlling completes one management cycle and improves planning in the next.
Explain how controlling helps accomplish goals, judge the accuracy of standards and use resources efficiently.
Explain how controlling improves employee motivation, ensures order and discipline and facilitates coordination.
Identify the difficulty of setting quantitative standards and the little control over external factors as limitations.
Explain resistance from employees and the cost of control systems as limitations of controlling.
Explain why planning is a prerequisite for controlling and controlling is blind without planning.
Evaluate the statement that planning is looking ahead and controlling is looking back.

topics.title: Controlling process: setting, measuring and comparing

concepts.learning_objective: State the five steps of the controlling process in their correct order.
Distinguish quantitative and qualitative standards and set standards in measurable terms.
Apply techniques of measuring actual performance and compare it with standards to find deviations.

topics.title: Analysing deviations and taking corrective action

concepts.learning_objective: Explain critical point control as focusing control on key result areas.
Apply management by exception to decide which deviations need managerial attention.
Decide the corrective action needed when deviations go beyond the acceptable range.
